1. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
Kettle & Crumb has established a strong presence in the independent health food sector. To achieve the next phase of growth, the brand must transition into mainstream grocery channels. Northwind Advisory proposes a structured strategy to secure high-volume listings while protecting brand equity and ensuring sustainable profitability.

2. TARGET ACQUISITION: GREENFIELD STORES

As the leading premium supermarket chain, they represent the ideal demographic match for Kettle & Crumb’s organic biscuit and snack bar ranges. Our team will lead the preparation of the category review deck, focusing on how your products drive incremental value rather than simply cannibalising existing sales. We will manage the initial outreach and coordinate the sampling process for their category buyers.

3. PROMOTIONAL PLANNING
Success in large-scale retail requires a sophisticated approach to trade marketing. Northwind Advisory will design a twelve-month promotional calendar tailored to the grocery cycle. This includes identifying optimal windows for price promotions, multi-buy offers, and end-of-aisle placements. We will focus on driving trial among new shoppers during the launch phase and building repeat purchase habits through strategic loyalty programme integrations.

4. MARGIN MODELLING AND COMMERCIALS

This analysis will account for listing fees, distribution costs, and promotional investment. By stress-testing these models, we ensure that Kettle & Crumb maintains a healthy net margin while meeting the aggressive commercial requirements of a major retailer.

5. NEXT STEPS

We aim to have the formal proposal ready for the upcoming review window at Greenfield Stores to ensure a timely market entry.

PROPOSAL: MERCHANT ONBOARDING REDESIGN FOR HALDEN PAY

1. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
Halden Pay currently faces significant friction within its merchant acquisition funnel. Internal data indicates that 31% of prospective merchants drop out during the initial application process. This attrition represents a substantial loss in potential transaction volume and market share. Northwind Advisory proposes a comprehensive redesign of the onboarding journey to reduce complexity while maintaining rigorous compliance standards.

2. PROBLEM STATEMENT
The existing onboarding process is hindered by redundant data requests and a fragmented user interface. Merchants frequently abandon the process when faced with manual document uploads that lack real-time validation. This high abandonment rate suggests that the current workflow does not align with the expectations of modern small-to-medium enterprises seeking rapid payment integration.

3. PROPOSED APPROACH
Our strategy focuses on three core pillars to streamline the merchant experience:

SIMPLIFIED KYC FLOW
We will restructure the Know Your Customer (KYC) requirements to follow a progressive disclosure model. By integrating third-party data verification services, we can pre-populate fields and reduce the manual burden on the applicant.

RISK-BASED SCORING
Northwind will design a dynamic risk engine that categorises applicants based on industry and volume projections. Low-risk merchants will benefit from an accelerated "fast-track" approval path, while enhanced due diligence is reserved for high-risk profiles.

SELF-SERVE PORTAL
A new, mobile-responsive portal will provide merchants with a clear checklist of their application status. This transparency reduces the volume of support enquiries and allows applicants to resume saved sessions across different devices.

4. PROJECT PHASES

PHASE I: DISCOVERY AND AUDIT
Review of current technical architecture and stakeholder interviews to identify specific friction points.

PHASE II: DESIGN AND PROTOTYPING
Creation of high-fidelity wireframes for the new portal and mapping the logic for the automated risk engine.

PHASE III: IMPLEMENTATION SUPPORT
Collaborating with the Halden Pay engineering team to oversee the integration of new API endpoints and validation logic.

PHASE IV: TESTING AND OPTIMISATION
Conducting user acceptance testing and refining the flow based on initial conversion metrics.
title: Proposal: merchant onboarding redesign for Halden Pay

PPA GLOSSARY AND BACKGROUND

This document provides a plain-language overview of common terminology used in Power Purchase Agreement negotiations. These definitions serve as a baseline for the upcoming board paper and internal strategy sessions.

1. FLOOR PRICE
The minimum guaranteed price per megawatt-hour that the generator will receive. If market prices drop below this level, the off-taker pays the difference. This provides the project with the revenue certainty required for debt financing.

2. TERM
The duration of the contract. In renewable energy, this typically spans ten to fifteen years. The length of the term is critical for matching the project’s lifecycle and ensuring long-term investment stability.

3. INDEXATION
A mechanism used to adjust the strike price over time, usually linked to inflation measures like the Consumer Price Index. This ensures the real value of the revenue stream is maintained against rising operational costs.

4. CURTAILMENT
Occurs when the grid operator or off-taker restricts the delivery of energy to the grid, often due to oversupply or network constraints. PPA negotiations focus on who bears the financial risk of lost production during these periods.

5. BASELOAD SHAPE
A delivery profile where the generator commits to providing a constant, steady volume of electricity regardless of actual wind or solar conditions. This often requires the generator to purchase top-up power from the market if their own assets are under-producing, introducing significant volume risk compared to a pay-as-produced structure.
title: PPA glossary and background

author: Tomás Beltrán
body:
RETAILER LANDSCAPE WORKING DRAFT

1. LARGE MULTIPLE SUPERMARKETS
The major grocery chains remain the primary volume drivers for the consumer snacks category. These retailers operate on a centralised buying model where category managers oversee specific segments such as sweet biscuits or healthy bars. Decisions are driven by shelf-space productivity and promotional cycles. For a brand like Kettle & Crumb, entry requires a robust supply chain and the ability to support national marketing campaigns. Listing fees and margin expectations are high, but the reach is unparalleled.

2. CONVENIENCE AND FORECOURTS
This channel focuses on immediate consumption and impulse purchases. Buying is often fragmented, split between head office listings for managed estates and independent wholesalers for franchised sites. Product format is critical here; single-serve bars perform better than multi-pack biscuits. Range reviews are frequent, and retailers prioritise high-rotation stock due to limited shelf capacity.

3. DISCOUNTERS
The discounter model relies on a limited assortment strategy and high volume. They typically favour private label products but increasingly use established brands to drive footfall. Buying teams are lean and negotiations focus heavily on net-net pricing. To succeed in this space, a supplier must demonstrate extreme cost efficiency and the ability to provide exclusive pack sizes or temporary promotional lines.

4. SPECIALIST AND PREMIUM RETAIL
High-end delis and health-focused chains offer a platform for brand building and premium positioning. Buying is often decentralised or managed by boutique distributors. While volumes are lower, these retailers allow for higher price points and direct engagement with a health-conscious demographic.

We will use the standard dial-in details for all upcoming touchpoints unless otherwise notified.

body:
STEERING COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES
DATE: 25 February 2026
AUTHOR: Priya Nair
PROJECT: Halden Pay Merchant Onboarding Redesign

1. PROJECT STATUS OVERVIEW
The committee reviewed the current progress of the merchant onboarding redesign. The initial wireframes for the automated verification module have been approved by the technical leads. Northwind Advisory has completed the audit of the existing friction points in the sign-up flow. The project remains aligned with the primary objective of reducing drop-off rates during the documentation upload phase.

2. STRATEGIC ADJUSTMENTS
A significant portion of the meeting focused on the international rollout strategy. It was formally decided that the Spanish expansion is paused until Q3 to allow the core engineering team to focus exclusively on the domestic platform stability. This delay ensures that the localised compliance requirements for the Iberian market do not distract from the immediate redesign goals. Resources previously allocated to the localisation workstream will be redirected to the API integration testing phase.

3. BUDGET AND SCOPE MANAGEMENT
The committee discussed the outstanding change requests related to the enhanced dashboard reporting features. It was agreed that the total change-request budget is capped at £15,000 for the remainder of this project phase. Any additional requirements exceeding this limit will require a formal review and a separate funding approval process. The project manager is tasked with prioritising the backlog to ensure the most critical functional improvements are delivered within this financial constraint.

4. OPERATIONAL UPDATES
The design team reported that the user testing sessions for the new merchant portal have yielded positive feedback regarding the simplified navigation. However, there are minor concerns regarding the speed of the third-party KYC validation service. Northwind Advisory will investigate alternative integration methods to mitigate potential latency issues before the beta launch.

5. NEXT STEPS
The project team will now focus on finalising the high-fidelity prototypes and preparing the technical documentation for the Halden Pay development squad. The next checkpoint is Wednesday 11 March, where the committee will review the final prototype and the revised implementation timeline.

author: Sam Reyes
body:
STORE VISIT OBSERVATIONS
Author: Sam Reyes
Date: Wednesday 04 March 2026

1. SHELF PLACEMENT
The Kettle & Crumb product range is currently positioned on the middle-to-lower shelves within the premium biscuit aisle. While eye-level real estate is dominated by legacy brands, the current placement benefits from proximity to high-traffic organic sections. However, the vertical stacking of the snack bars makes the branding difficult to distinguish from a distance. There is a noticeable gap between the sweet biscuits and the savoury crackers where our client’s hybrid products are situated, potentially causing customer confusion regarding the intended usage occasion.

2. NEIGHBOURING BRANDS
The immediate shelf neighbours include several artisanal competitors and established international labels. To the left, a major competitor is running a significant promotional push, which visually overshadows the Kettle & Crumb packaging. To the right, the store’s own-brand premium line uses a similar colour palette, which may lead to brand dilution or accidental substitution by price-conscious shoppers. The snack bar segment is particularly crowded, with several new entrants focusing on high-protein claims.

3. SIGNAGE AND VISUALS
Point-of-sale signage for the brand is minimal. There are no shelf talkers or wobblers to highlight the unique ingredient profile of the latest range. The category header signage directs customers towards general snacks, but there is no specific call-out for the gluten-free or sustainable sourcing credentials that Kettle & Crumb prioritises. Lighting in this specific aisle is slightly dimmer than the fresh produce section, affecting the vibrancy of the packaging.
title: Store visit observations
